history. 412U.S. at 739. Yet the Comptroller General’s roster of statutory

same time that the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act assigns to the

Congress could assign the Comptroller General’s function to an 
administrator not subject to presidential removal at will, he thought it 
“eminently reasonable and proper for Congress to vest the budget-cutting 
authority in an officer who is to the greatest degree possible nonpartisan

therefore may be rehed upon not to allow his calculations to be colored by
